requirement: Implement a test isolation runner (run_with_patched_clock) that patches target module attributes for the duration of a test and guarantees 100% restoration of the original target object even when the test raises an exception.
skeleton: RemoteClockService with staticmethod get_timestamp(), run_with_patched_clock helper, and verify_clock_unpolluted verification.

rationale.teaches: A patch helper that starts a patcher with the requested value and stops it in a finally block, so the original attribute is restored even when the test raises.
rationale.why: A patch that is never stopped pollutes every later test but passes its own. The fixture runs a raising test and then checks the class attribute is the original.

candidates.why_wrong: The patcher is never stopped, so the patched timestamp leaks into every later test.
stop runs after the test without finally, so a raising test leaves the patch active.
finally is replaced by except and re-raise, so a passing test leaves the patch active.
start is called where stop should be, so the patch is applied twice and never removed.
The patched return value is hardcoded to 1000, so the requested target_time is ignored.
